title.zh: 房子为什么能立住不倒
title.en: Why Don’t Buildings Fall Down?

content.zh: 房子的重量顺着柱子、墙一直传到地基，再传到地上。柱子直、地基稳，重量就稳稳地被传下去，房子就立住了。
content.en: A building’s weight passes down through columns and walls into the foundations and then the ground. Straight columns and firm ground keep it standing.

title.zh: 桥为什么能跨过河
title.en: How Can a Bridge Cross a River?

content.zh: 桥把自身的重量和车子的重量，沿着桥面传到两端的桥墩，再压进地里。拱形、斜拉、梁式，都是想办法把力传走。
content.en: A bridge carries its own weight and the traffic along the deck to piers at each end, then into the ground. Arches, cables and beams all move the force along.

title.zh: 为什么高楼要打地基
title.en: Why Do Tall Buildings Need Foundations?

content.zh: 高楼很重，直接放在松土上会慢慢陷下去、歪掉。往地下打进深深的桩，才能把重量传到下面坚硬的土层或岩石上。
content.en: A tall building is heavy; on soft soil it would sink and tilt. Deep piles are driven down to carry the weight to hard soil or rock below.

title.zh: 隧道是怎么挖出来的
title.en: How Are Tunnels Dug?

content.zh: 工人用巨大的盾构机往前推，前面的刀盘把土和石头切下来运走，后面立刻拼好一圈圈管片，撑住挖出来的洞壁。
content.en: Workers push a huge tunnelling machine forward. Its cutting head slices soil and rock, which is carried away, and ring-shaped segments are fitted behind to hold the walls.

title.zh: 飞机为什么能飞上天
title.en: Why Can Aeroplanes Fly?

content.zh: 机翼上面鼓、下面平。空气从上面走得快、压力小，下面走得慢、压力大，上下一压一托，就把飞机托了起来。
content.en: A wing is curved on top and flat beneath. Air moves faster over the top, lowering pressure there, while higher pressure below pushes the wing up.

title.zh: 高铁为什么跑得那么快
title.en: Why Do High-Speed Trains Go So Fast?

content.zh: 高铁车身做成流线型减少空气阻力，还用电力驱动，轮子沿着专用轨道跑，没有红绿灯和交叉路口，所以又快又稳。
content.en: Its streamlined body cuts air resistance, electric motors drive it, and it runs on dedicated track with no lights or junctions, so it is both fast and steady.

title.zh: 地铁为什么在地下跑
title.en: Why Do Subways Run Underground?

content.zh: 城市地面又挤又堵，把铁路修到地下就不占马路，也不受天气影响。专门的车厢和隧道，让很多人能同时进城。
content.en: City streets are crowded, so putting the railway underground saves road space and avoids weather. Dedicated tunnels and carriages carry many people at once.

title.zh: 自行车骑起来为什么不会倒
title.en: Why Doesn’t a Bicycle Fall Over?

content.zh: 车轮转起来时，转动的车轮想保持原来的方向，就像陀螺一样立着不倒。骑得越快，这股稳住的力量就越大。
content.en: A spinning wheel tends to keep its direction, like a spinning top staying upright. The faster you ride, the stronger this steadying effect.

title.zh: 电梯为什么不会掉下来
title.en: Why Don’t Lifts Fall?

content.zh: 电梯有粗粗的钢丝绳拉着。就算绳子全断了，导轨上还有安全钳会死死咬住导轨，把轿厢夹住停住。
content.en: Lifts hang from thick steel ropes. Even if they all broke, safety clamps on the guide rails would grip tightly and hold the car in place.

title.zh: 金字塔是怎么建起来的
title.en: How Were the Pyramids Built?

content.zh: 古埃及人用铜凿子凿出巨石，靠斜坡和木撬一点点往上拖，一层一层堆上去。几万个人工，干了几十年的活儿。
content.en: Workers cut huge blocks with copper tools and dragged them up ramps on wooden sledges, layer by layer. Tens of thousands of people worked for decades.

title.zh: 为什么马路要有红绿灯
title.en: Why Do Roads Have Traffic Lights?

content.zh: 路口的车和人要从不同方向过，都一起走就会撞上。红绿灯给每个方向轮流一段时间，路口就有秩序又安全。
content.en: Traffic and people cross from different directions at a junction, and going together causes crashes. Lights give each direction a turn, keeping it orderly and safe.

title.zh: 汽车轮胎上为什么有花纹
title.en: Why Do Tyres Have Tread?

content.zh: 花纹能把雨天路面上的水排走，让橡胶直接碰到地面不打滑；还能增加摩擦，刹车和转弯时更稳当。
content.en: Tread channels water away on wet roads so the rubber grips the ground instead of sliding. It also adds friction, making braking and turning steadier.

title.zh: 城市里为什么要修立交桥
title.en: Why Do Cities Build Flyovers?

content.zh: 路口的车太多，平交会让大家互相等。让一层走直行、一层拐弯，谁也不挡谁，路就通得快多了。
content.en: Too many cars meet at one crossing and each has to wait. Send straight traffic on one level and turning traffic on another, and nobody blocks anybody.

title.zh: 铁轨下面为什么要铺石子
title.en: Why Are There Stones Under Railway Tracks?

content.zh: 那些碎石能把火车的重压摊开，不让路基下沉；还能排水、固定枕木，顺便把杂草压住。
content.en: The crushed stone spreads a train's weight so the track bed does not sink. It also drains water, holds the sleepers in place and keeps weeds down.

title.zh: 火车为什么要在铁轨上跑
title.en: Why Do Trains Run on Rails?

content.zh: 钢轮压在钢轨上，摩擦力很小，拉几十节车厢也不费劲。铁轨还负责把车稳稳地引向前方。
content.en: Steel wheels on steel rails meet with very little friction, so one engine can pull dozens of carriages. The rails also steer the train firmly forward.

title.zh: 船头为什么做成尖的
title.en: Why Is the Bow of a Boat Pointed?

content.zh: 尖头能把水分开、减少阻力，船跑起来又快又省油。圆头的船推着水走，费劲得多。
content.en: A pointed bow splits the water and cuts drag, so the boat moves faster and uses less fuel. A blunt bow has to shove water aside, which is much harder work.

title.zh: 屋顶为什么要做成斜的
title.en: Why Are Roofs Sloped?

content.zh: 斜屋顶让雨水和雪顺着坡滑下去，不会积在顶上压坏房子，也不容易漏水。雨多的地方屋顶斜得更明显。
content.en: A slope lets rain and snow slide off instead of piling up and leaking in. Where rain is heavy, you will notice the roofs are steeper.

title.zh: 北方的房子墙为什么特别厚
title.en: Why Are Walls Thicker in the North?

content.zh: 厚墙像一件棉袄，冬天挡住寒气、留住屋里的热；夏天又挡住外面的热。暖气费也能省下不少。
content.en: A thick wall works like a coat: it keeps cold out and warmth in during winter, and keeps heat out in summer. It also cuts heating bills.

title.zh: 马路上为什么有一条凹凸的路
title.en: Why Is There a Bumpy Strip on the Pavement?

content.zh: 那是盲道，凸起的条纹和圆点用脚底就能感觉出来，指引视力不好的朋友往前走、在路口停下。
content.en: It is a tactile path. Raised lines and dots can be felt through the soles, guiding people with poor sight forward and telling them to stop at crossings.

title.zh: 高楼为什么用玻璃做外墙
title.en: Why Do Tall Buildings Have Glass Walls?

content.zh: 玻璃幕墙很轻，能减轻楼的重量；采光明亮又省电，还能把天空映在楼上，看着漂亮。
content.en: Glass walls are light, so they reduce the building's weight. They let in daylight, saving power, and mirror the sky, which looks striking.

title.zh: 有些大桥为什么拉着许多钢索
title.en: Why Do Some Bridges Have Many Cables?

content.zh: 斜拉桥用钢索把桥面吊在塔上，等于多了好几个支点，桥就能跨得更宽、用更少的桥墩。
content.en: On a cable-stayed bridge, steel cables hang the deck from towers, adding many supports so the span can be longer with fewer piers.

title.zh: 坐车为什么要系安全带
title.en: Why Must We Wear a Seat Belt?

content.zh: 车急刹时人还会往前冲，安全带把你稳稳拉住，不让你撞上挡风玻璃。这一拉能救很多人的命。
content.en: When a car stops suddenly your body keeps going. The belt holds you back so you do not hit the windscreen, and that simple strap saves many lives.

title.zh: 机场为什么建在城外
title.en: Why Are Airports Built Outside the City?

content.zh: 飞机起降要很长的跑道，还得留出安全的空地；再加上噪音大，放在城外对居民影响最小。
content.en: Take-off and landing need long runways and clear space for safety. Add the noise, and siting them outside town troubles the fewest people.

title.zh: 拱形门为什么特别结实
title.en: Why Is an Arch So Strong?

content.zh: 拱把上面的重量沿着弯弯的线传到两边地基上，石头之间互相挤压、越压越紧，所以能撑很久。
content.en: An arch carries weight down its curve into the ground at both sides. The stones press against each other and grip tighter under load, so arches last ages.

title.zh: 房子为什么要留窗户
title.en: Why Do Houses Have Windows?

content.zh: 窗户能采光通风，让屋里亮堂、空气新鲜。它还让人看得见外面，住着才不憋闷。
content.en: Windows bring light and air so rooms are bright and fresh, and they let you see outside, which keeps a home from feeling shut in.

title.zh: 高楼为什么还要有楼梯
title.en: Why Do Tall Buildings Still Have Stairs?

content.zh: 起火时电梯不能用，楼梯是唯一安全的逃生路。平时它也让人能走走，不必都挤电梯。
content.en: Lifts cannot be used in a fire, so stairs are the only safe way out, and day to day they let people walk instead of crowding into lifts.

title.zh: 为什么要有消防通道
title.en: Why Are There Fire Lanes?

content.zh: 消防通道让消防车能开到楼下、云梯能架起来。被车堵住的通道，会耽误救火救命的几分钟。
content.en: Fire lanes let engines reach the building and ladders be raised, and a lane blocked by parked cars costs precious minutes in an emergency.

title.zh: 高楼为什么要装避雷针
title.en: Why Do Tall Buildings Have Lightning Rods?

content.zh: 避雷针用金属把雷电引入地下，保护楼里的人和设备。它不是躲开雷，而是给雷修一条安全的路。
content.en: A rod carries lightning safely into the ground through metal, protecting people and equipment, and rather than avoiding the strike it gives it a safe path.

title.zh: 为什么桥面要留缝
title.en: Why Are There Gaps in a Bridge Deck?

content.zh: 天热时桥面会伸长，天冷会缩短。留一道缝给它伸缩，不然桥面会被自己挤裂。
content.en: The deck lengthens in heat and shortens in cold, so a gap lets it move freely, otherwise the bridge would crack under its own strain.

title.zh: 桥上为什么要有栏杆
title.en: Why Do Bridges Have Railings?

content.zh: 栏杆挡住人和车，不让他们掉下去；还能提醒司机桥的边缘在哪，夜里和雾天尤其重要。
content.en: Railings stop people and vehicles going over the edge and show drivers where the edge is, which matters most at night or in fog.

title.zh: 隧道里为什么要有通风口
title.en: Why Do Tunnels Need Vents?

content.zh: 隧道里空气不流通，汽车尾气会越积越多。通风口把脏空气换掉，也让火灾时能排烟。
content.en: Air cannot circulate in a tunnel so exhaust builds up, and vents swap in fresh air and carry smoke away in a fire.

title.zh: 高铁座位为什么没有安全带
title.en: Why Don't High-Speed Train Seats Have Belts?

content.zh: 列车减速平缓，很少急刹，坐在座位上就够安全。加上座椅能吸能挡，系安全带反而不方便逃生。
content.en: Trains slow gently and rarely stop suddenly, so sitting is safe enough, and with energy-absorbing seats a belt would only hinder escape.

title.zh: 高铁车窗为什么打不开
title.en: Why Can't Train Windows Be Opened?

content.zh: 时速几百公里时，开窗会让车厢内气压猛变，噪音惊人，还可能把东西吸出去。所以全程密封。
content.en: At hundreds of kilometres per hour an open window would swing the pressure, roar with noise and suck objects out, so the carriages stay sealed.

title.zh: 飞机窗户为什么是圆角的
title.en: Why Are Aeroplane Windows Rounded?

content.zh: 方角的窗会在角上集中应力，反复加压后容易裂开。圆角把力均匀分散，飞行就更安全。
content.en: Square corners concentrate stress and crack under repeated pressurising, while rounded corners spread the force evenly and keep flying safe.

title.zh: 坐飞机为什么要调成飞行模式
title.en: Why Use Flight Mode on a Plane?

content.zh: 手机会不断搜索信号，可能干扰飞机的导航和通讯。调成飞行模式就断了这些信号，大家更安全。
content.en: A phone keeps searching for signals, which may disturb the aircraft's navigation and communication, so flight mode stops those signals and keeps everyone safer.

title.zh: 飞机为什么要排队起飞
title.en: Why Do Planes Queue to Take Off?

content.zh: 跑道上一次只能有一架飞机，前一架起飞后还要等尾流散开。调度排队能保证间距，避免相撞。
content.en: Only one aircraft can use a runway at a time and the wake behind it must settle, so controllers space the departures to keep them safely apart.

title.zh: 机场为什么要安检
title.en: Why Is There Security at Airports?

content.zh: 安检是为了查出危险物品，不让它们带上飞机。飞机在空中无处可躲，所以这一关格外严格。
content.en: Security finds dangerous items before they get on board, and since an aircraft in flight has nowhere to turn, this check is especially strict.

title.zh: 汽车为什么要有后视镜
title.en: Why Do Cars Have Mirrors?

content.zh: 司机看不到正后方，后视镜帮他看清旁边和后面的车，变道和倒车全靠它，是重要的安全装置。
content.en: A driver cannot see straight behind, so mirrors show the sides and rear, and changing lanes or reversing depends on them for safety.

title.zh: 安全气囊有什么用
title.en: What Is an Airbag For?

content.zh: 撞车时气囊在几十分之一秒内弹出，垫住头和胸，避免撞上方向盘。它是安全带的搭档，不是替代品。
content.en: In a crash the bag inflates in a fraction of a second, cushioning head and chest from the wheel, and it works with the seat belt rather than instead of it.

title.zh: 马路上为什么要有斑马线
title.en: Why Are There Zebra Crossings?

content.zh: 斑马线的条纹非常醒目，提醒司机前面有人要过街，也告诉行人该从哪里走。
content.en: The bright stripes warn drivers that people are crossing and show pedestrians where to walk, making both sides aware of each other.

title.zh: 马路为什么要限速
title.en: Why Do Roads Have Speed Limits?

content.zh: 速度越快，看得越窄、刹车距离越长，撞上时的力也越大。限速就是给所有人留出反应的余地。
content.en: The faster you go the narrower your view, the longer the stopping distance and the harder the impact, so limits leave everyone room to react.

title.zh: 骑摩托车为什么要戴头盔
title.en: Why Wear a Helmet on a Motorbike?

content.zh: 骑车人没有车壳保护，摔倒时头部最容易受伤。头盔的外壳和内衬能吸收撞击，救下很多命。
content.en: A rider has no shell around them and the head is most at risk in a fall, so a helmet's shell and lining absorb the blow and save many lives.

title.zh: 自行车为什么要有车铃
title.en: Why Do Bicycles Have Bells?

content.zh: 铃声能提醒行人和其他车辆注意，尤其在转角和窄路上。它是自行车上最简单的沟通工具。
content.en: A bell warns pedestrians and other traffic, especially at corners and on narrow paths, and it is the simplest way a cyclist can communicate.

title.zh: 晚上骑车为什么要装反光板
title.en: Why Fit Reflectors When Cycling at Night?

content.zh: 反光板能把车灯的光原路反射回去，司机远远就能看见你。自己不发光，却最省电也最可靠。
content.en: Reflectors send a car's headlight beam straight back, so drivers see you from far off, and though they make no light of their own they are reliable and need no power.

title.zh: 船身上为什么有刻度线
title.en: Why Are There Marks on a Ship's Hull?

content.zh: 那是吃水线，表示船装了多少货、吃水多深。装太满超过标记，船就有危险。
content.en: They are load lines showing how deep the ship sits and how much it carries, and loading past the mark puts the ship in danger.

title.zh: 港口为什么建在弯进去的海湾
title.en: Why Are Ports Built in Sheltered Bays?

content.zh: 弯进去的海湾风浪小，船停靠装卸都安全。水深合适、背后有陆地挡风的地方最适合建港。
content.en: A curving bay keeps waves down so ships can load and unload safely, and deep water with land to break the wind makes the best harbour.

title.zh: 为什么要开凿运河
title.en: Why Are Canals Dug?

content.zh: 运河把两条水路连起来，船就不用绕远路。巴拿马运河让船少走几千公里，省时又省燃料。
content.en: A canal joins two waterways so ships avoid long detours, and the Panama Canal saves thousands of kilometres, which saves both time and fuel.

title.zh: 环岛有什么用
title.en: What Is a Roundabout For?

content.zh: 车辆绕着中心单向行驶，不用等红绿灯，也不用横穿对向车流，事故更少、通行更顺。
content.en: Traffic circles one way around a centre with no lights to wait for and no crossing of oncoming cars, so there are fewer crashes and smoother flow.

title.zh: 马路上为什么要装路灯
title.en: Why Are There Street Lights?

content.zh: 路灯让司机看清路面和行人，也让人晚上敢出门。亮堂的街道还能减少事故和犯罪。
content.en: Lights let drivers see the road and people, make going out at night feel safe, and brighter streets mean fewer accidents and less crime.

title.zh: 为什么要修人行道
title.en: Why Are There Pavements?

content.zh: 人行道把人和车分开，走路的人不必跟汽车抢路，安全得多。它也是轮椅和婴儿车的空间。
content.en: A pavement keeps people apart from traffic so walkers do not compete with cars, and it also gives room for wheelchairs and prams.

title.zh: 屋檐为什么要伸出来
title.en: Why Do Eaves Stick Out?

content.zh: 伸出的屋檐把雨水甩离墙脚，免得淋湿墙面、泡坏地基。夏天还能给墙遮一片阴凉。
content.en: Overhanging eaves throw rain clear of the wall so it does not soak the base, and in summer they shade the wall from the sun.

title.zh: 水上的房子是怎么盖的
title.en: How Are Houses Built on Water?

content.zh: 先把木桩或水泥柱打进水底，再在上面架平台盖房。威尼斯和侗族的水上民居都是这么建的。
content.en: Piles of timber or concrete are driven into the bed, a platform is built on top and the house goes up, as in Venice and the stilt homes of southern China.

title.zh: 蒙古包为什么是圆形的
title.en: Why Is a Yurt Round?

content.zh: 圆形最抗风，风从哪边来都能顺着滑过去；同样材料围出的空间也最大，拆装搬运还方便。
content.en: A round shape resists wind best, letting it slip past from any side, encloses the most space for the material used, and is easy to take down and carry.

title.zh: 为什么有人住在窑洞里
title.en: Why Do Some People Live in Cave Dwellings?

content.zh: 黄土高原的土层又厚又结实，挖出的窑洞冬暖夏凉，还省建材。这是就地取材的老智慧。
content.en: The thick loess soil is firm enough to dig into, and cave homes stay warm in winter and cool in summer while using little material, an old local wisdom.

title.zh: 房子为什么要朝南建
title.en: Why Are Houses Built Facing South?

content.zh: 在北半球，朝南的房子冬天能晒到太阳取暖，夏天阳光高、晒不进屋，一年都舒服。
content.en: In the northern hemisphere a south-facing house catches winter sun for warmth while summer sun rides high and stays out, so it is comfortable all year.

title.zh: 地铁站为什么装屏蔽门
title.en: Why Do Metro Stations Have Platform Doors?

content.zh: 屏蔽门把人和轨道隔开，防止跌落和跳轨，还能挡住列车带来的风，让站台更凉快。
content.en: Platform doors separate people from the track, stopping falls and keeping out the wind trains push ahead, which also cools the platform.

title.zh: 马路上为什么要立路牌
title.en: Why Are There Road Signs?

content.zh: 路牌提前告诉司机前面是什么路、有什么危险，让人有时间准备。认得路牌，出行才安全。
content.en: Signs tell drivers in advance what is ahead and what dangers lie there, giving time to prepare, and knowing them keeps travel safe.

title.zh: 城市地下有什么
title.en: What Is Under a City?

content.zh: 地下埋着自来水管、下水道、电缆、燃气管和地铁，像一座看不见的城市。规划好了，地面才运转顺畅。
content.en: Water mains, sewers, cables, gas pipes and the metro lie beneath, an invisible city, and planning it well keeps everything above running smoothly.

title.zh: 为什么要修人行天桥
title.en: Why Build Footbridges?

content.zh: 天桥让行人从车流上方走过，不必横穿马路，既安全又不打断车流。车多的路口最适合建。
content.en: Footbridges take people over traffic so they need not cross the road, which is safer and keeps cars moving, and they suit the busiest junctions.

title.zh: 路面上的标线有什么用
title.en: What Are Road Markings For?

content.zh: 白线和黄线把路分成车道，告诉车该走哪、能不能变道。夜里和雨天，它们比什么都管用。
content.en: White and yellow lines divide the road into lanes and say where to drive and whether you may change lane, and at night or in rain nothing works better.
